# Two templates written as Go string literals in one file, parsed with
# different delimiters.
#
# Delimiters belong to the source that was parsed, not to the file holding it,
# and one .go file can hold several parsed sources. Reading either literal with
# the other's pair yields a tree with no actions in it.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

var templates = template.Must(
	template.Must(
		template.New("t").Delims("[[", "]]").Parse(`[[define "square"]]Hello, [[.Name]]![[end]]`),
	).Delims("{{", "}}").Parse(`{{define "curly"}}Bye, {{.Name}}.{{end}}`),
)

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Square(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "square", page)
}

func Curly(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "curly", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestSquare(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Square(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("square = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestCurly(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Curly(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Bye, World."; got != want {
		t.Errorf("curly = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
